people.label: Michael Herrera
people.sub: Former US Marine who says that in 2009, during humanitarian and security operations after an Indonesian earthquake, he and his unit encountered a large craft being loaded by non-uniformed armed personnel
people.narrative: Michael Herrera is a claimant whose account has reached two official records without him ever having testified, and the distinction is the whole reason this node is carefully worded. He has never been a witness at a congressional hearing. His name appears exactly once across the printed records of the three modern House UAP hearings: on 9 September 2025 Rep. Eric Burlison moved a document about him into the record, describing it as testimony given to him by Dr. Steven Greer, and the chair admitted it without objection. Separately, AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I carries at page 29 an anonymised one-sentence summary of a 2009 foreign humanitarian-mission account that matches his public account on year, mission type and scene. AARO names nobody and maintains the anonymisation key itself, so the identification of that interviewee as Herrera is an inference and is carried here as Tier 3, not as a fact. His own account is on the public record in a dated artefact, a Shawn Ryan Show appearance of 17 July 2023. No service record, no DD-214 and no corroborating squadmate was opened. What makes him a node is proximity to a claim that two official records touch, not credibility: he held no programme office and no clearance is documented anywhere.
people.tierRationale: Authored C. Proximity, not credibility. He held no programme office, no documented clearance, and the account is a single unwitnessed personal experience. What distinguishes him from an ordinary claimant is that his account reaches two official records, anonymously in AARO Volume I and by motion in a hearing record.

claims.text: The printed record of the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing of 9 September 2025 carries this colloquy. Rep. Eric Burlison: 'Madam Chair, I also have further witnesses of courageous individuals. It was given to me by Dr. Steven Greer, including Michael Herrera and his testimony. We have Roderick Castle and his testimony; Randy Anderson, his testimony; Steven Digna, and others, three others, all saying similar things to what the witnesses today have said, and I would like to enter that into the record as well.' Chairwoman Luna: 'No objection.' What this documents is that a member moved a document about him into a hearing record and sourced it to Steven Greer. It does not document that he testified, was sworn, or appeared.

He is on no congressional witness list. The committee-published witness lists for 26 July 2023 (event 116282), 13 November 2024 (event 117722) and 9 September 2025 name him nowhere, and the printed records of all three hearings contain his name exactly once in total, in the Burlison colloquy.

AARO's 'Report on the Historical Record of U.S. Government Involvement with Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP), Volume I', February 2024, carries at page 29, in Section V 'Assessment of Interviewee Claims of USG Involvement in Hidden UAP Programs', this sentence: 'An interviewee who is a former U.S. service member said that in 2009, while participating in a humanitarian and security mission in a foreign country, he encountered U.S. Special Forces loading containers onto a large extraterrestrial spacecraft.' The sentence is AARO's summary of an interview, not a quotation of the interviewee, and it names nobody.
claims.source: AARO Historical Record Report Volume I, p. 29, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dod/AARO_Historical_Record_Report_Volume_1_2024.pdf , 2024-02

claims.text: The same report states the anonymisation rule that is why the page 29 sentence names nobody: 'AARO generated random numbers and assigned one to each interviewee. AARO maintains the key, which is stored and handled in a secure manner to protect each interviewee's privacy.' It also gives the scale and the tiering: 'As of September 17, 2023, AARO interviewed approximately 30 individuals', with Tier 1 interviewees being 'those who have spoken with congressional staff or Members of Congress and have been subsequently referred to AARO'.
claims.source: AARO Historical Record Report Volume I, p. 28, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dod/AARO_Historical_Record_Report_Volume_1_2024.pdf , 2024-02

claims.text: The identification of AARO's page 29 interviewee as Michael Herrera is an INFERENCE and this node carries it as one. It matches his public account on year, on mission type and on the described scene. No opened record makes the link, AARO names nobody, and Herrera is not named anywhere in the report.
claims.source: stated inference from the AARO Volume I page 29 summary and his Shawn Ryan Show account

claims.text: His own account is on the public record in a dated artefact: 'Michael Herrera - US Marine Encounters UFO Black Ops Human Trafficking Operation | SRS #66 (Part 1)', Shawn Ryan Show, premiered 17 July 2023, runtime 1:26:50. The channel's own description reads: 'Former Marine Michael Herrera tells all in part one of this three part series. Herrera and his team were tasked with responding to a major earthquake and tsunami in Indonesia providing overwatch and logistical support. Little did they know--they would come face to face with a UAP / UFO and be ambushed by an unmarked shadow unit of operators.' This is a man saying a thing on a dated recording, and nothing more.

people.label: Jason Sands
people.sub: Retired US Air Force master sergeant, by his own account and by one named critic's account, who since 2024 has claimed knowledge of a classified non-human-technology programme
people.narrative: Jason Sands is the thinnest node on this board and it is built deliberately thin. Not one primary record about him was opened: no personnel record, no filed document, no official mention. He is a real, distinct, identifiable person, because two independent openable artefacts converge on the same man with the same stated service history, and one of those two is a critic's. That is enough to justify a node under the same discipline that justified Brad Sorensen in the ARV thread, and it is not enough for a single Tier 1 claim. The node exists for two reasons. Its sceptical claim records a named critic's itemisation of what Sands asserts, which is the most substantive material about him in the open. And its last claim exists specifically to stop two attributes entering this board by repetition: that he appears in a named documentary, and that he has given testimony to Congress, the ICIG or AARO. Neither is established by any opened record.
people.tierRationale: Authored C. Proximity, not credibility, and this is the thinnest node here. No primary record about him was opened and every claim is Tier 2 or Tier 3.

claims.text: On The Joe Rogan Experience #2264, appearing with Lenval Logan, Sands stated his service in his own words: 'I'm a retired master sergeant from the air Force. Worked 22 years, retired 2007. Started off as an airframe guy, ended up in intel.' A named man on a recording, self-reporting. The episode's publication date was not established from any page opened.

Brian Dunning, writing on 13 May 2024, gives an independent account of the same service: Air Force from 1985 to 2007, working in aircraft structural maintenance and then as an Electronic System Security Assessment specialist, retiring as a Master Sergeant, in a role involving 'collecting, analyzing, and processing Department of Defense telecommunications' and identifying 'critical information potentially compromised'. A named writer's dated account, not a personnel record.

The two accounts above agree on rank, on end date and on length of service, and 1985 to 2007 is 22 years. That is weak convergence on the service claim only, from two sources with no shared method, and it is not a service record. Nothing else about him converges at all.
claims.source: stated inference from the Joe Rogan Experience transcript and the Dunning piece

claims.text: The disputing material, from the same named critic on the same date. Brian Dunning itemises Sands's claims as including that the Wilson-Davis memo is genuine, which Dunning calls an 'obviously hoaxed' document; that alien spacecraft use electromagnetic propulsion; that aliens cooperated in reverse-engineering programmes; that a 'blue alien species' exists with whom humans can communicate telepathically; that non-physical aliens assist intelligence programmes; and that underground bases house aliens and that time travel and remote viewing are real. Dunning further states that Sands initially claimed involvement with the Navy's UAP Task Force and later contradicted himself, and that Sands has not run into any trouble violating DoD confidentiality protocols.

The two attributes most often used to make Sands significant, that he appears in James Fox's documentary 'The Program' and that he gave testimony to Congress, the ICIG or AARO, are NOT established by any opened record. The film was not viewed and the one trade report on it was behind a paywall gateway. No congressional witness list names him. This claim exists to stop those attributes entering the board by repetition.
claims.source: stated inference; the committee witness lists were opened 2026-09-18 and do not name him

That is an institutional position inside the question rather than adjacent to it. This node is deliberately incomplete: it carries what the 17 May 2022 transcript establishes and nothing more. His career, tenure dates and subsequent positions have not been researched, and a later pass should treat the node as unfinished rather than as settled.

claims.text: The University of Colorado Boulder publishes her as a Lecturer in its Lockheed Martin Engineering Management Program, previously an adjunct instructor in the Engineering Leadership Program (2022) and Scholar in Residence to the Engineering Management Program (2023). The same page gives her career as a 20-year Naval career as an F/A-18F strike fighter pilot, with combat deployments supporting Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation Enduring Freedom, a final yearlong assignment as an infrastructure reconstruction engineer in Ghazni, Afghanistan, and a Bronze Star and Air Combat Medal. Prior teaching posts: Naval Science instructor across a Washington DC consortium of Georgetown, George Washington, Howard and Catholic universities, and Military Professor at the US Naval Academy, Department of Leadership, Ethics and Law. Education: BS Civil Engineering, George Washington University; Defense Language Institute certification in Dari; MBA, GW School of Business. This is an employer's published biography of its own lecturer, not a service record.

CBS News, 60 Minutes, correspondent Bill Whitaker, published 16 May 2021, states that Dietrich, a former F/A-18F pilot, 'has never before spoken publicly about what she saw that day'. The same report quotes her: 'It was unidentified. And that's why it was so unsettling to us. Because we weren't expecting it. We couldn't classify it'; 'No predictable movement, no predictable trajectory'; and 'I felt the vulnerability of not having anything to defend ourselves. And then I felt confused when it disappeared.' This dates the start of her public record to 16 May 2021 on the network's own assertion.

In sworn testimony at the 26 July 2023 House Oversight subcommittee hearing, David Fravor placed her in the chain of who re-opened the 2004 case: 'Years later, I was contacted by the other pilot, Alex Dietrich, and asked if I would been contacted and I said no, but I am willing to talk.' Tier 1 for the fact that a sworn witness said this on that date; the underlying sequence is his account.

In sworn testimony at the 13 November 2024 House Oversight joint hearing, Tim Gallaudet named her while alleging AARO pressure on him: 'In addition, they tried to have me question very valid UAP reports like the Tic Tac incident, even coming to a--stating possibly that the Tic Tac was American technology. And then, of course, if you ask David Fravor or Alex Dietrich, the two witnesses, they were convinced it was otherwise.' Tier 1 for the fact that he said it under oath. The allegation about AARO's conduct is his word and caps at Tier 2 as a claim about the world.

claims.text: The biography Fravor filed with the subcommittee for the 26 July 2023 hearing, held in the House Committee Repository under event 116282, reads in full: 'David Fravor is a retired naval pilot and Commander of VFA-41 also known as The Black Aces. He is one of the primary witness in the 2004 USS Nimitz UFO incident. He was featured in the 2008 PBS documentary Carrier and has been interviewed on Joe Rogan's podcast The Joe Rogan Experience. Fravor joined the military at the age of 17. He has a career spanning 24 years, 18 of which was as a Navy pilot. He had completed five tours to the Persian Gulf starting after Operation Desert Storm. He commanded a squadron of 12 airplanes consisting of 330 people. Fravor retired in 2006.' The grammatical slip 'one of the primary witness' is in the original. This is a document filed with a committee and held in its repository, which is what makes it Tier 1. It is a witness-supplied biography, not a Navy service record.

The testimony was sworn, and the printed record carries the mechanism. Chairman Grothman: 'Pursuant to Committee Rule 9(g), the witnesses will please stand and raise their right hands. Do you solemnly swear to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, so help you God? [Witnesses are sworn.] Mr. Grothman. Let the record show that all the witnesses answered in the affirmative.'

Under oath he gave the radar picture of the 14 November 2004 intercept, in answer to Rep. Langworthy: 'The Princeton tracked it. The Nimitz tracked it. The E2 tracked it. We never saw it on our radars. Our fire control radars never picked it up. The other airplane that took the video did get it on a radar. As soon as it tried to lock it, it jammed the radar, spit the lock and he rapidly switched over to the targeting pod, which you can do in the F-18.'

Under oath he gave the reason the aircrew were airborne at all: 'We were at a work up with all the battle groups. So, we integrate the ships with the carrier, the airwing with the carrier, and we start working. So, we were doing an air to air defense to hone not only our skills but those of the USS Princeton when they had been tracking them for 2 weeks. The problem was that there was never manned aircraft airborne when they were tracking them and this was the first day and, unfortunately, we were the ones airborne and went and saw it.'

Under oath he gave the chain by which the case reached investigators and then the public: 'It was not until 2009, until Jay Stratton had contacted me to investigate. Unbeknownst to all, he was part of the ATIP program in the Pentagon led by Lue Elizondo. There was an unofficial official report that came out that is now on the internet. Years later, I was contacted by the other pilot, Alex Dietrich, and asked if I would been contacted and I said no, but I am willing to talk. I was contacted by Mr. Elizondo, and we talked for a short period of time.' This is the provenance chain in the words of the witness, under oath.

Asked by Rep. Langworthy 'is it true that you saw, in your words, a 40-foot flying Tic Tac shaped object?', he answered under oath: 'That is correct. For some people that cannot--know what a Tic Tac is it is a giant flying propane tank.'

entities.label: House Intelligence subcommittee hearing, 17 May 2022: 'Unidentified Aerial Phenomena'
entities.sub: The first open congressional hearing on this subject in over fifty years, taking testimony from Under Secretary Moultrie and Deputy Director Bray
entities.desc: The House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, Subcommittee on Counterterrorism, Counterintelligence, and Counterproliferation, meeting at 9:00 a.m. in Room HVC-210 of the Capitol Visitor Center with Rep. Andre Carson presiding, took testimony from Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security Ronald S. Moultrie and Deputy Director of Naval Intelligence Scott W. Bray. It is the first open congressional hearing on unidentified aerial phenomena in more than fifty years, and it is the hearing from which the 2023, 2024 and 2025 Oversight sequence descends. The board carried a node for every other congressional UAP hearing of the modern era and not this one, which is the gap this node closes.
entities.tierRationale: Authored A, matching the other modern congressional UAP hearing nodes. Its full transcript is openable at congress.gov and it is the origin of the modern hearing sequence.

claims.text: The transcript's own caption block reads: 'UNIDENTIFIED AERIAL PHENOMENA / Tuesday, May 17, 2022 / U.S. House of Representatives, / Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, / Subcommittee on Counterterrorism, Counterintelligence, / and Counterproliferation, / Washington, D.C.' It records that 'The subcommittee met, pursuant to call, at 9:00 a.m., in Room HVC-210, Capitol Visitor Center, the Hon. Andre Carson [chairman of the subcommittee] presiding', with Representatives Carson, Schiff, Welch, Himes, Krishnamoorthi, Wenstrup, Crawford, Gallagher, Mullin and LaHood present.

Carson stated the hearing's premise on the record: 'More than 50 years ago, the U.S. Government ended Project Blue Book... In 2017, we learned for the first time that the Department of Defense had quietly restarted a similar organization, tracking what we now call unidentified aerial phenomena, or UAPs. Last year Congress rewrote the charter for that organization, now called the Airborne Object Identification and Management Synchronization Group, or AOIMSG for short. Today we will bring that organization out of the shadows.'

Carson put the organisational status question to the witnesses on the record: 'First, we need you to update us on the status of AOIMSG. The legislation creating it was passed in December. The deadline for implementation is fast approaching, but the group does not even have a named director.'

gaps.text: No service record, DD-214 or unit assignment for Michael Herrera was opened. His Marine Corps service and his presence on the 2009 Indonesian humanitarian mission are self-stated. A personnel or unit record would move several claims on that node from Tier 2 to Tier 1, or refute them.

The 'Memorandum for Record' Michael Herrera says he obtained from AARO was NOT OPENED. Only a search-engine paraphrase of a social-media post describing it was found. If genuine and openable it would bear directly on the Tier 3 identification of him with the AARO Volume I page 29 interviewee.

The publication date of The Joe Rogan Experience #2264 with Lenval Logan and Jason Sands was not established from any opened page, so the Sands service claim has no dated artefact of its own beyond the Dunning piece of 13 May 2024.
NOT ONE primary record about Jason Sands was opened: no personnel record, no filed document, no official mention. Every claim on that node is Tier 2 or Tier 3 and the node is built on that basis.

Neither Ronald Moultrie's nor Scott Bray's career, tenure dates or subsequent positions were researched. Both nodes carry only what the 17 May 2022 transcript establishes and are deliberately incomplete.

Roderick Castle, Randy Anderson, Steven Digna and Matthew Brown are all named in the opened printed record of 9 September 2025 and none is on the board. None was researched. A node built from a single name in a member's remarks would be padding, so they are carried here by name as the next pass's candidates.
congress.gov returned HTTP 403 for both Senate hearing records during the roster sweep, so those roster rows rest on existing board nodes plus search metadata rather than on opened primaries.
David Fravor's Truth in Testimony form for 26 July 2023 is an image-only scan and no OCR was available, so its contents are not carried.
James Fox's documentary 'The Program' was not viewed and the one trade report on it was behind a paywall gateway. No node is created for it and nothing here asserts who appears in it.
